DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer` claims to solve a monetary/latency/balance objective via `_objective()`, but `_solve_greedy()` never consults that objective or any proxy for `c_m` / `tau_m`; it sorts only by current load fraction. In a verified two-model counterexample with equal limits but radically different cost and latency, the solver assigns the task to the first-listed expensive/slow model. This means the implementation is not actually optimizing the stated GAP objective, so returned allocations can be arbitrarily worse than a feasible alternative.

DESCRIPTION: The “pre-dispatch probabilistic feasibility” extension is implemented only as an optional helper and is never enforced in the normal allocation path. `get_allocation()` calls `LoadBalancer.solve()` directly, and `solve()` ignores `L_std` entirely. I verified this with a model at `L=10000, L_std=3000`: `get_allocation()` assigns a 10k-token task, while `check_dispatch_feasibility()` on the same input returns `(False, 0.5)`. So the advertised feasibility guard is advisory only and can be bypassed by standard use of the manager.

DESCRIPTION: The adaptive fingerprint loop updates only `DynamicManager._live_fingerprints`; `FailureHandler` keeps its own frozen `self.models` map from construction time and `_expected_performance()` always reads from that stale pool. I verified that changing a model’s live fingerprint changes `get_live_models()` but leaves `_expected_performance(model_id)` unchanged. Underperformance detection is therefore judging later rounds against initial capability estimates, not the live state the rest of the manager is using.

DESCRIPTION: The code says findings are grouped by an equivalence relation, but `_compute_equivalence_classes()` actually uses single-linkage connected components over pairwise threshold hits. That is a stricter bug than the already-noted fragile similarity function: even with a perfect oracle, `A≈B` and `B≈C` will merge `A` and `C` into one class even when `A` and `C` are below `tau_sim`. I verified this with a custom similarity function that makes only `A-B` and `B-C` similar; the detector still collapses all three into one class. This can falsely suppress novelty and inflate convergence downstream.

DESCRIPTION: When a model has `L <= 0`, both `_objective()` and `_balanced()` replace `load / L` with `0.0` instead of treating it as infeasible or effectively infinite. In a verified single-model example with `L=0` and a forced assignment, `solve()` emits an F1 overload warning but still returns `balanced=True`. That makes the diagnostic outputs internally contradictory: the allocation is infeasible, but the manager reports it as perfectly balanced because the impossible load fraction was zeroed out.
